series_title: What If You Woke Up a Random Size Every Day?
part1_title: What If You Woke Up a Random Size Every Day? Part 1: Half an Inch
part1_script:
[0.0s · BEDROOM, dawn. Bug's-eye low camera; Meatball fills the frame, standing on a giant pillow] MEATBALL: Today I woke up half an inch tall. | Title pill 'What If You Woke Up a Random Size Every Day?' + PART 1 · DAY 1 top-left · SIZE wheel beside Meatball spins and lands: 1/2 IN, subtitle SILVERFISH SIZE (ding) · top-right KYLE PANIC bar, 3 grey segments
[3.0s · BEDROOM, pillow] MEATBALL: Tomorrow? Random. | SIZE wheel gives one teaser wobble
[4.0s · NIGHTSTAND. The phone lies flat like a court, with Meatball standing on the baseline] MEATBALL: My phone is now a tennis court. | —
[6.6s · FLASHBACK cut 1/3, sepia. Kyle's sneakers drag a couch in from the curb] MEATBALL: Kyle dragged home a free curb couch. | —
[9.3s · FLASHBACK cut 2/3. Cardboard sign taped to a cushion] MEATBALL: The sign said, "DO NOT NAP." | sign text pops
[11.6s · FLASHBACK cut 3/3. Meatball asleep on the couch, snore bubble] MEATBALL: I napped. | —
[12.6s · BEDROOM FLOOR, carpet macro. A long, low shadow of many legs slides in] MEATBALL: A house centipede walks in. | —
[14.6s · BEDROOM FLOOR. Doug enters long and low (body 2-3x Meatball's length, legs fanned wide, never towering)] MEATBALL: Thirty legs. Zero knocking. | chip: 15 PAIRS · PENN STATE
[16.3s · BEDROOM FLOOR, Doug face-to-face] DOUG: Morning. | —
[17.0s · BEDROOM FLOOR, Meatball deadpan to camera] MEATBALL: Under an inch, bugs talk. Great. | —
[19.3s · BEDROOM FLOOR] DOUG: I'm Doug. I eat roaches, spiders, silverfish. | roach, spider, silverfish icons pop in one per word (reuse assets)
[22.0s · BEDROOM FLOOR. A silverfish icon slides in beside Meatball, the same length] MEATBALL: I'm silverfish-sized. | SIZE subtitle SILVERFISH SIZE flashes red
[23.0s · BEDROOM FLOOR] DOUG: Relax. What even are you? | —
[25.0s · BEDROOM FLOOR, Meatball points at himself] MEATBALL: A meatball. Everybody eats me. | —
[27.0s · BEDROOM FLOOR] DOUG: Not me. I'm pest control. Unpaid. | each menu icon gets a check mark
[29.3s · BEDROOM FLOOR] DOUG: Harmless to people. Penn State says so. | fact card: PENN STATE EXTENSION: house centipedes "are harmless"
[32.0s · BEDROOM FLOOR] DOUG: In writing. | card stamps down
[33.0s · BEDROOM DOORWAY. Giant sneakers fill the frame; the camera tilts up and keeps going] MEATBALL: Kyle walks in. He's a skyscraper. | —
[35.3s · DOORWAY, Kyle's head far above, mouth wide] KYLE: CENTIPEDE! | KYLE PANIC slams full (3/3)
[36.0s · DOORWAY] KYLE: That's it. Exterminator. Saturday. | the panic bar flips into a red stamp: EXTERMINATOR: 5 DAYS (alarm sting)
[37.7s · BEDROOM FLOOR. Doug darts under the bed, fast] DOUG: I eat his roaches. For free. | —
[40.0s · BEDROOM FLOOR. Meatball waves both arms with a tiny squeak SFX; the sneakers turn away] MEATBALL: I yell for help. Kyle says, "Bless you." | —
[43.0s · UNDER THE BED. Dim, dust bunnies like boulders] DOUG: That couch rerolls you every sunrise. | SIZE wheel ticks once
[45.3s · UNDER THE BED] DOUG: The last guy found a cure. | —
[47.6s · UNDER THE BED] MEATBALL: Where is he? | —
[49.0s · UNDER THE BED. Slow push into a small hole in the baseboard. In the dark is a tiny SIZE dial with cracked glass and a frozen needle] MEATBALL: Doug stares at the wall. | no label; the frozen dial is the season's mystery (Walter's)
[51.0s · MATTRESS macro, zooming into the weave] DOUG: Tomorrow could be dust-mite size. | —
[53.0s · MATTRESS. Dust mites drift among skin flakes] DOUG: They live in mattresses. They eat dead skin. | chip: WSU EXTENSION
[55.9s · MATTRESS. The mites slowly turn to face the camera] DOUG: They don't bite. They wait for you to shed. | —
[59.2s · UNDER THE BED] MEATBALL: What are the odds? | —
[60.9s · FULL-SCREEN WHEEL: 20 equal, countable slices; one red slice labeled DUST MITE] DOUG: One in twenty. | ODDS 1 IN 20 pill appears under SIZE
[62.2s · UNDER THE BED] MEATBALL: So, basically never. | —
[63.6s · UNDER THE BED, Doug turns slowly to Meatball] DOUG: So, basically Tuesday. | —
[64.9s · UNDER THE BED, night. Meatball asleep on the carpet; the wheel spins in its display] MEATBALL: I fall asleep. The wheel spins. | SIZE spinning, slowing and clicking
[67.3s · UNDER THE BED, first dawn light. The wheel stops on the red slice] MEATBALL: Dust-mite size. | DAY 1 → DAY 2 · SIZE lands 0.01 IN · DUST MITE (red flash) · EXTERMINATOR: 4 DAYS
[68.3s · BEDROOM FLOOR. A robot vacuum's light blinks on and it rotates toward the bed] MEATBALL: Kyle's robot vacuum just turned on. | —
[70.6s · UNDER THE BED. The vacuum's headlight floods in and the brushes spin up. The camera stays bug's-eye, so Meatball still fills the foreground] MEATBALL: It starts under the bed. | hard cut to black · PART 2 card (ends about 72.6s)
[TOTALS: 181 spoken words · longest line 9 words · about 72.6 s at 150 wpm · voice at 0.0 s · Meatball gets the last word]
voices: MEATBALL (first-person narrator AND in-scene hero): edge-tts en-US-AndrewMultilingualNeural, rate +10% (channel rule for Shorts/TikToks, Nolan 10/24). Every narration line is Meatball's inner voice. This meets 'Meatball is the star': first person, he reacts to every reveal and gets the last word. The second-person 'What if YOU' hook is carried by the title pill only. His in-world shout ('I yell for help') is NOT voiced: play a short pitched-up squeak SFX under the narration line, so he 'speaks' in-world sparingly.

DOUG (house centipede; deadpan, unpaid in-house pest control and mentor): en-US-ChristopherNeural, rate -8%, pitch -6Hz, flat delivery with a half-beat pause before each button line ('In writing.' / 'So, basically Tuesday.').

KYLE (roommate, giant human seen as sneakers and legs): en-US-EricNeural, rate +12%, pitch +4Hz. edge-tts cannot scream, so build 'CENTIPEDE!' from Eric at +20% rate and +10Hz, layered with a short scream SFX, and keep the clip under 0.8 s.

Later parts (first appearance in brackets): CRUMB the dust mite [P2]: en-US-AnaNeural, +5%. FUZZ the carpet beetle larva [P3]: en-US-BrianMultilingualNeural, +5%, mumbly. VLAD the bed bug [P3]: en-US-SteffanNeural, -5%, smooth. WALTER 'the last guy' [P5]: en-US-BrianMultilingualNeural, -12%, -4Hz (keep Fuzz and Walter apart by rate and pitch). LINDA the cellar spider [P5]: en-US-AriaNeural, -5%. PROFESSOR PAGE the silverfish [P5]: en-US-GuyNeural, -15%. THE EXTERMINATOR [P6]: en-US-AndrewNeural (not Multilingual), -5%, tired. Each character gets exactly one voice for the whole season.
counters: TITLE PILL: 'What If You Woke Up a Random Size Every Day?' + PART N label. The 16:9 scene sits letterboxed in the 9:16 frame on dark navy, the same layout as the reference.
DAY N, top-left. Ticks at each sunrise; Day 1 = Monday. In Part 1 it goes DAY 1 → DAY 2 at 67.3 s, the 'Dust-mite size.' beat.

SIZE WHEEL beside Meatball, our version of the reference's IQ display. It is a small 20-slice prize wheel with a readout. The readout is INCHES ONLY (no mm), with a creature subtitle taken from sourced sizes. Part 1: it lands 1/2 IN · SILVERFISH SIZE at 0.0 s, flashes red at 22.0 s, spins at 64.9 s and lands 0.01 IN · DUST MITE in red at 67.3 s. The slices are equal and countable, so viewers can verify '1 in 20' and argue about it in the comments. Slices with a creature label (use only these): 0.01 in DUST MITE (red), 0.2 in BED BUG / APPLE SEED, 0.25 in MOUSE GAP, 1/2 in SILVERFISH, 1.5 in CENTIPEDE BODY. The season also needs 3 ft 11 in (Part 4) and 6 ft 1 in (Part 6). Fill the remaining 13 slices with plain numbers only, no creature names.
ODDS pill: '1 IN 20' pops in under SIZE at 60.9 s, while the wheel is shown full-screen with its single red slice.

TOP-RIGHT, Part 1: a 3-segment KYLE PANIC bar (reuse g.meter). At Kyle's 'CENTIPEDE!' (35.3 s) it slams full and flips into a red countdown, EXTERMINATOR: 5 DAYS (36.0 s). It ticks to 4 DAYS at the Day 2 sunrise. The countdown is earned on screen, not just announced. Later parts: the countdown sits top-right with the panic bar underneath. Whenever the bar fills, Kyle makes a bad decision: Part 4, the couch goes to the curb. It reads TODAY in Part 6.

Source chips: small grey pills, 1.5 s each: '15 PAIRS · PENN STATE' at 14.6 s, a full fact card 'PENN STATE EXTENSION: house centipedes are harmless' at 29.3-33.0 s, and 'WSU EXTENSION' at 53.0 s. They build trust, and the 'In writing.' joke lands on the card.
Mystery prop with no label: Walter's tiny SIZE dial (cracked glass, frozen needle) seen through the baseboard hole at 49.0 s. It pays off in Part 5.
From Part 3: a FRIENDS / ENEMIES column under the countdown. Doug starts in FRIENDS. Vlad the bed bug's icon sits stuck on '?' between the columns all season (running gag).
scenes_needed: BEDROOM, dawn + night (EXISTING: drawn_rooms SCENES 'bedroom'). Needs a giant-pillow foreground (EXISTING actors 'pillow_face' / 'sleeper' as a base) and a nightstand with a phone lying flat. NEW small prop: the phone.
BEDROOM FLOOR / CARPET MACRO (EXISTING: drawn_rooms 'fibers' as the carpet-pile macro) for every bug's-eye floor shot (12.6-42.9 s).

FLASHBACK: CURB COUCH, sepia, 3 cuts at most, 5 s total (NEW: a curb couch with a cardboard 'DO NOT NAP' sign, plus a plain curb/sidewalk strip). The couch is a recurring prop: it is also the Part 3 cushions and the Part 6 curb.
BEDROOM DOORWAY with giant sneakers and a tilt-up to Kyle (EXISTING: drawn_cast ACTORS 'person', shot as feet and legs, with the head only in the 35.3 s scream wide).

UNDER THE BED: dim, dust bunnies, bed skirt (a bedroom variant with the lights down). NEW small props: a mouse-gap-sized hole in the baseboard and a tiny cracked SIZE dial (re-use the counter's dial art with a crack overlay).
MATTRESS MACRO (EXISTING: drawn_rooms 'fibers' retinted as mattress ticking; 'skin' as a backup) with dust mites.
FULL-SCREEN ODDS WHEEL: a 20-slice graphic (NEW, made by enlarging the SIZE wheel counter art; no separate asset).
ROBOT VACUUM 'DUSTIN' (NEW prop, needed for the whole season): a round body, one blinking status light, a headlight, spinning side brushes. Part 2 needs a matching dustbin interior.

CREATURES, all EXISTING actors: house_centipede (Doug), roach + silverfish + one harmless spider icon (use jumping_spider or cellar_spider, NOT widow) for Doug's menu, dust_mite + mite_crowd + skin_flake for the mattress. Meatball mascot with red cap in every shot.

LATER PARTS, existing where noted: dustbin interior (NEW, P2-P3); couch-cushion interior with bed bugs (bed-bug creature from the drawn-house bed-bugs episodes, P3); carpet beetle larva (existing carpet-beetle asset, P3); living room + kitchen (EXISTING drawn_habitats 'kitchen', P4); cereal letters on the floor (g.prop, P4); inside-the-wall cross-section (NEW, can reuse the basement wall texture, P5); basement (EXISTING drawn_assets 'basement', P5); cellar spider + web (EXISTING drawn_actors 'cellar_spider', 'web', P5); silverfish Professor Page with a nibbled notebook page (EXISTING silverfish + drawn_rooms 'book', P5); rainy curb at night + garbage truck silhouette (NEW, P5-P6); exterminator (drawn_cast 'person' recolored with a uniform and clipboard, P6); a second SIZE wheel floating beside Kyle (counter art, P6).
sources: Penn State Extension, 'House Centipedes', https://extension.psu.edu/house-centipedes. Verified live 2026-11-03: 'Adult house centipedes have 15 pairs of legs'; body 'one to one and one-half inches in length', 'three to four inches in length (including legs and antennae)'; 'feed on silverfish, firebrats, carpet beetle larvae, cockroaches, spiders, and other small arthropods'; 'While they are fast and have long legs, which may frighten some people, they are harmless'; 'During the daytime, the centipedes inhabit dark, damp locations in the home.' The page is SILENT on bites, so never say 'never bites'. Supports P1 lines 'Thirty legs', 'I eat roaches, spiders, silverfish', 'Harmless to people. Penn State says so', Doug darting away fast, the long-and-low drawing scale, and P6's 'fix the damp'.

Washington State University Extension PestSense, 'House dust mites', https://pestsense.cahnrs.wsu.edu/fact-sheet/house-dust-mites/. Verified live 2026-11-03: 'extremely small (up to 0.5 mm)'; 'principally found in cotton-stuffed mattresses and furniture' (no mention of pillows, so the script says mattresses); 'feed primarily on human skin cells that have sloughed off and pet dander'; 'They do not bite'; 'prefer humid environments'. Supports P1 'dust-mite size' (0.01 in ≈ 0.25 mm, inside WSU's range), 'They live in mattresses. They eat dead skin. They don't bite.', and P2's Crumb.

UC IPM Pest Notes, 'Silverfish and Firebrats' (Pub. 7475), https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/PESTNOTES/pn7475.html. Verified live 2026-11-03: common silverfish 'about 1/2 inch long, although it can grow as long as 3/4 inch'; prefer 'paper with glue or paste'; 'can live for several months without nourishment'; nocturnal. Supports P1's '1/2 IN · SILVERFISH SIZE' label and 'I'm silverfish-sized', plus P5's Professor Page ('In March. It was mostly glue.').

U.S. EPA, 'Bed Bugs: Appearance and Life Cycle', https://www.epa.gov/bedbugs/bed-bugs-appearance-and-life-cycle. Verified live 2026-11-03: adults 'about the size of an apple seed (5-7 mm or 3/16 - 1/4 inch long)'. Supports P3's 0.2 in · APPLE SEED (0.2 in ≈ 5 mm, inside EPA's range). This is the current page; ignore the older 3/8 in PDF.

U.S. EPA, 'Protecting Your Home from Bed Bugs', https://www.epa.gov/bedbugs/protecting-your-home-bed-bugs. Verified live 2026-11-03: 'Check secondhand furniture, beds and couches for any signs of bed bug infestation before bringing them home.' The page says nothing about 'curbside' furniture, so P4 quotes this wording ('the EPA literally says to check secondhand couches') instead of the pilot's unsupported 'EPA warns about curbside furniture'.
CDC, 'About Bed Bugs', https://www.cdc.gov/bed-bugs/about/index.html. Verified live 2026-11-03: 'Bed bugs are not known to spread diseases to people'; size range 1-7 mm. Supports P4.

UC IPM, 'Carpet Beetles', https://ipm.ucanr.edu/home-and-landscape/carpet-beetles/ (Pest Notes 7436). Verified live 2026-11-03: 'Carpet beetle adults do not feed on fabrics but seek out pollen and nectar'; larvae feed on 'wool, silk, leather, fur', feathers, pet hair; 'They don't feed on synthetic fibers.' Supports P3's Fuzz ('wool phase', 'Polyester? Gross.').

UC IPM, 'House Mouse', https://ipm.ucanr.edu/home-and-landscape/house-mouse/. Verified live 2026-11-03: 'House mice can squeeze under gaps ¼ inch tall, and through openings 3/8 inch wide'; mainly nocturnal. P5 says 'squeeze under a quarter-inch gap', the exact wording, not 'through a 1/4-inch hole'.

UC Riverside Entomology, 'Are daddy longlegs really the most venomous spiders in the world?', https://entomology.ucr.edu/news/2022/01/14/are-daddy-longlegs-really-most-venomous-spiders-world (short answer: 'no'; cellar spiders are 'Definitely not the most toxic spider in the world', per Rick Vetter). Also UCR, https://spiders.ucr.edu/daddy-long-legs: 'There is no scientific basis for the supposition that they are deadly.' Both verified live 2026-11-03. Supports P5's Linda myth-bust.

Missouri Department of Conservation field guide, 'Cellar Spiders', https://mdc.mo.gov/discover-nature/field-guide/cellar-spiders. Verified live 2026-11-03: they 'eat other small arthropods (insects, spiders, and so forth)'; the venom legend 'purports that cellar spiders have more potent venom than any other spider. But studies have shown this is not at all the case; in fact, pholcid venom is comparatively rather mild.' Supports P5's 'cellar spiders eat other spiders'. This replaces the pilot's unsupported 'black widows included (Burke Museum)' line, which is CUT.

Iowa State University Extension, Yard and Garden, 'Long-Bodied Cellar Spider' (Laura Iles, Feb 4, 2009), https://yardandgarden.extension.iastate.edu/article/2009/2-4/cellarspider.html. Verified live 2026-11-03: 'they eat insect pests, house centipedes, and other things we do not like in our homes'; 'not poisonous to humans'; concentrated in basements. Supports P5's reason Doug won't go in the wall.

Fiction, labeled as fiction (the 'What If' frame and the AI-content label): the curb couch, daily size rerolls, talking bugs, the 'under an inch, bugs talk' rule, the 1-in-20 odds, Walter, the cure, and the second wheel. Scale math (not bug facts): Meatball's normal height is fixed at 6 ft, so half an inch is 1/144 scale. A 6 x 3 in phone becomes 72 x 36 ft, and a doubles tennis court is 78 x 36 ft, so 'My phone is now a tennis court' is literally close. Kyle at 6 ft becomes about 864 ft ('skyscraper').

Season 2 bank, already vetted by the channel and the judges: Vetter & Barger 2002, J. Med. Entomol. 39(6):948-951, https://doi.org/10.1603/0022-2585-39.6.948 (2,055 brown recluses in one Kansas home over six months, no bites; say only 'a Kansas home'). CDC NIOSH Venomous Spiders, https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/outdoor-workers/about/venomous-spiders.html (say 'on the CDC's venomous-spider list', not 'have a CDC page'). Clemson HGIC 'Sowbugs & Pillbugs', https://hgic.clemson.edu/?p=5940 (crustaceans; 'dry out and die quickly inside a house'). Not used in Part 1.
parts_2_to_6: PART 2: 'Dust-Mite Size'. DAY 2 (Tue) · SIZE 0.01 IN · DUST MITE · EXTERMINATOR 4 DAYS · Under the bed → mattress. It opens on the cliffhanger. At this size Dustin (Kyle's robot vacuum) is weather: you ride its exhaust gust into the bed skirt and climb into the mattress. There you meet Crumb, a dust mite your exact size. He confirms mites live in mattresses, eat shed skin, love humidity and don't bite (WSU Extension): 'You're not prey. You're catering.' Doug can't even see you and stands guard at the bed leg. Button two-hander: Doug: 'Where are you?' Crumb: 'He's the speck.' Doug: 'They're all specks.' CLIFFHANGER: Kyle strips the bed and shakes the sheet out over the floor. You fall, Dustin is parked right underneath, and you land in the pitch-dark dustbin, buried in lint. Something right next to you is chewing. Meatball (last word): 'Please be lint.'

PART 3: 'Apple Seed'. DAY 3 (Wed) · SIZE 0.2 IN · APPLE SEED · 3 DAYS · Dustbin → the curb couch. The chewer is Fuzz, a carpet beetle larva working through Kyle's wool-sock lint: 'I'm in my wool phase.' Carpet beetle larvae eat wool, fur, feathers and pet hair but not synthetic fibers, and adults eat pollen and nectar (UC IPM): 'Polyester? Gross.' (Fix for the pilot's contrived bin dump: Dustin's dock sits under the curb couch.) The bin lid cracks, and you climb out and up into the cushions to dodge Kyle's sneakers. The cushions are full of bed bugs, each apple-seed size (EPA: 3/16 to 1/4 inch), which is exactly your size. Vlad leans in: 'Finally. Someone at eye level.' The FRIENDS/ENEMIES column debuts and Vlad's icon sticks on '?'. Vlad: 'Relax. You're a meatball. I have standards.' CLIFFHANGER: Kyle naps on the couch, right on top of your cushion. Sunrise. The wheel lands on its biggest slice, 3 FT 11 IN, and you're still under the cushion. Meatball: 'This is going to be awkward.' (Kyle napping on the couch is the setup for the Season 2 twist.)

PART 4: 'Too Big To Hear Them'. DAY 4 (Thu) · SIZE 3 FT 11 IN · 2 DAYS · Living room → kitchen. You burst out from under the cushion, launching Kyle, and his PANIC bar fills in one scream. Above an inch the bugs go silent (the Part 1 rule), so Doug's mouth moves and nothing comes out. Meatball: 'For once in my life, I'm not the food.' You finally warn Kyle about the couch. Bed bugs aren't known to spread disease to people (CDC), but the EPA literally says to check secondhand couches for bed bugs before bringing them home (EPA wording, no 'curbside' claim). Kyle: 'So the couch is a timeshare.' The panic bar maxes again, and Kyle decides the couch goes back to the curb tonight. CLIFFHANGER: on the kitchen floor Doug has spelled a message in cereal, COUCH = CURE. KEEP IT, and Kyle is already carrying the couch out the door. Meatball: 'Kyle. Kyle. KYLE.'

PART 5: 'The Last Guy'. DAY 5 (Fri) · SIZE 0.25 IN · MOUSE GAP · 1 DAY · Inside the wall → basement. House mice squeeze under gaps a quarter inch tall (UC IPM), and today so do you, through the baseboard hole Doug stared at in Part 1. Doug won't come in, because Linda the cellar spider lives there. Cellar spiders eat other spiders (Missouri Dept. of Conservation) and even house centipedes (Iowa State Extension). Doug: 'I'll wait out here. Forever.' Linda insists she's the world's most venomous spider. Meatball myth-busts her on brand: there's no scientific basis for it, and pholcid venom is comparatively mild (UC Riverside Entomology; MDC). Linda: 'Rude. Accurate. Rude.' Inside, you find Walter, 'the last guy', tiny since 2019, holding the cracked, frozen SIZE dial from Part 1. The cure is one more night on the couch before it's gone. But the last page of Walter's notes is missing, and Professor Page the silverfish confesses: 'I ate it. In March. It was mostly glue.' (UC IPM: silverfish prefer paper with glue or paste and can live several months without food.) CLIFFHANGER: the couch is on the curb in the rain, and the garbage truck comes at 7 a.m. Walter: 'Also... I never technically finished the cure.' Page: 'Step two was on that page.' Meatball: 'There was a step TWO?'

PART 6: 'Pest Control Day'. DAY 6 (Sat) · SIZE ??? · EXTERMINATOR: TODAY · Curb → bedroom. You sleep on the soaked curb couch, and at dawn the wheel lands on 6 FT 1 IN. Cured? The exterminator arrives and is NOT the villain. He confirms the bed bugs are in the curb couch (no pesticide or treatment specifics on screen), then tells Kyle the centipede is eating his pests. House centipedes spend the day in dark, damp spots in the home (Penn State Extension), so the advice is to fix the damp, not Doug. Doug's icon moves to FRIENDS, Vlad stays on '?', and Kyle's PANIC bar empties for the first time all season. CLIFFHANGER: your SIZE wheel, which was supposed to stop, starts spinning again. So does a second wheel nobody noticed, floating next to KYLE, who napped on the couch in Part 3. The exterminator stares at it and sighs: 'Oh no. Not again.' Meatball (last word): 'Again?' Season 2 hook: the reroll has jumped to Kyle, and the exterminator has met this couch before.
production_notes:
WHY THIS PILOT: 'What If You Woke Up a Random Size Every Day?' won both judges' totals (67 and 66 vs 65/61 and 60/57). Like the reference's IQ number, the random daily SIZE is the mini-twist each part, and each size picks that part's co-star from our existing 'Things Living In Your House' library.

GRAFTS APPLIED:
(1) Runner-up C: first-person Meatball narration, to follow Nolan's 10/24 'Meatball is the star' order. Second person stays in the title pill only.
(2) C: the 'narrator who is food' persona: 'A meatball. Everybody eats me.' in P1 and 'For once in my life, I'm not the food.' in P4.
(3) C: odds made visible and countable as a 20-slice wheel with one red DUST MITE slice.
(4) C: Kyle's PANIC meter earns the exterminator countdown on screen and later drives the couch-to-curb decision.
(5) C: Walter's cracked, frozen dial planted visually in P1 at 49.0 s.
(6) C: the second wheel on Kyle as the Season 2 engine.
(7) A: the FRIENDS/ENEMIES column with Vlad stuck on '?'.
(8) A: Professor Page the silverfish ate the cure page ('It was mostly glue.'). This gives Walter's 'never finished the cure' a real cause.
(9) A: one two-hander button per part. P1's 'basically never / basically Tuesday' is deliberately NOT a copy of the reference's 'Fine. / It is not fine.'

FIXES vs the winning pilot:
- Line 1 no longer needs a +10% rate hack. It opens on the concrete 'Today I woke up half an inch tall.' with the wheel already landing and the title pill carrying the premise at frame 0.
- SIZE is inches-only (no mm mixing) with creature subtitles.
- Doug is drawn long and low (body 2-3x Meatball's length), not 'towering'.
- The flashback is 3 cuts and about 6 s.
- The P3 bin dump is replaced by Dustin's dock under the couch.
- P4's EPA line now quotes EPA's actual 'check secondhand furniture, beds and couches' wording.
- P5's unsupported 'black widows included (Burke)' line is cut. It is replaced by MDC ('eat other ... spiders') plus Iowa State Extension ('house centipedes'). MDC does mention cellar spiders capturing black-widow-genus spiders, but it stays out of the script to avoid fear framing.
- The mouse line uses UC IPM's exact 'squeeze under gaps 1/4 inch tall'.
- Dust mites are said to live in 'mattresses' (WSU names no pillows).
- 'Harmless' is kept exactly as Penn State says it, never upgraded to 'never bites'.
- The bed bug size uses the current EPA page (apple seed, 5-7 mm / 3/16-1/4 in).
- Every Part 1 bug line was re-verified live on 2026-11-03: Penn State, WSU, UC IPM x3, EPA x2, CDC, UCR x2, MDC, Iowa State. The UMich BioKIDS cellar-spider page returned 503 and is not cited.

TIMING: 181 words, about 72.6 s at 150 wpm, voice from 0.0 s, longest line 9 words, a new beat or visual change every 1-3 s, and an escalation about every 5-10 s (the size reveal, then the couch, Doug, Kyle, the exterminator, the last guy, the odds, and the land-plus-vacuum ending). The channel's Andrew +10% reads faster, about 66-70 s, which still clears the TikTok 60 s Creator Rewards floor. If a render comes in under 61 s, drop to +5% rather than adding words. The YouTube Short posts at full length.

CAMERA RULE: every shot is bug's-eye, so the world scales and Meatball stays the biggest thing in frame, including at dust-mite size, where he fills the foreground and the vacuum fills the background.
